source_text:
Σωζέσθω οὖν ἡμῶν ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ὑποτασσέσθω ἕκαστος τῷ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, καθὼς ἐτέθη ἐν τῷ χαρίσματι αὐτοῦ.
ὁ ἰσχυρὸς τημελείτω τὸν ἀσθενῆ, ὁ δὲ ἀσθενὴς ἐντρεπέσθω τὸν ἰσχυρόν: ὁ πλούσιος ἐπιχορηγείτω τῷ πτωχῷ, ὁ δὲ πτωχὸς εὐχαριστείτω τῷ θεῷ, ὅτι ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ, δἰ οὗ ἀναπληρωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὸ ὑστέρημα: ὁ σοφὸς ἐνδεικνύσθω τὴν σοφίαν αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐν λόγοις, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς: ὁ ταπεινοφρονῶν μὴ ἑαυτῷ μαρτυρείτω, ἀλλ’ ἐάτω ὑφ̓ ἑτέρου ἑαυτὸν μαρτυρεῖσθαι: ὁ ἁγνὸς ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ μὴ ἀλαζονευέσθω, γινώσκων ὅτι ἕτερός ἐστιν ὁ ἐπιχορηγῶν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν.
ἀναλογισώμεθα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἐκ ποίας ὕλης ἐγενήθημεν, ποῖοι καὶ τίνες εἰσήλθαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ἐκ ποίου τάφου καὶ σκότους ὁ πλάσας ἡμᾶς καὶ δημιουργήσας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον αὐτοῦ, προετοιμάσας τὰς εὐεργεσίας αὐτοῦ, πρὶν ἡμᾶς γεννηθῆναι.
ταῦτα οὖν πάντα ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔχοντες ὀφείλομεν κατὰ πάντα εὐχαριστεῖν αὐτῷ: ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Mutual care and gratitude in the body
orientation: Clement is applying the image of the body to the Corinthian church, urging each member to act within their God-given gift and to care for one another.
pass_a_gloss: Let be saved therefore our whole body in Christ Jesus, and let submit each one to the neighbor of him, just as he was placed in the gift of him. The strong let care for the weak, and the weak let respect the strong; the rich let supply to the poor, and the poor let give thanks to God, because he gave to him, through whom may be filled up of him the lack; the wise let show the wisdom of him not in words, but in works good; the one being humble not to himself let bear witness, but let allow by another himself to be witnessed; the pure in the flesh not let boast, knowing that another is the one supplying to him the self-control. Let us consider therefore, brothers, from what matter we were made, what sort and who we entered into the world, from what tomb and darkness the one having formed us and created [us] brought [us] into the world of him, having prepared beforehand the benefits of him, before us to be born. These things therefore all from him having we owe in all things to give thanks to him; to whom the glory to the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.term: Σωζέσθω οὖν ἡμῶν ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ
choices.english: Let our whole body be saved in Christ Jesus
choices.why: The passive imperative with the body as subject is best rendered as a passive English imperative; 'whole' preserves the emphasis on totality.
rejected: Let the whole body of us be preserved in Christ Jesus
Our whole body must be saved in Christ Jesus

choices.english: let each one submit to his neighbor
choices.why: The glossary term 'submission' (ὑποταγή) is the noun form; the verb here is the same root, so 'submit' keeps the connection to the letter's key theme.
rejected: let each one be subject to his neighbor
let each one obey his neighbor

choices.term: καθὼς ἐτέθη ἐν τῷ χαρίσματι αὐτοῦ
choices.english: just as he was placed in his gift
choices.why: The passive of τίθημι ('was placed') echoes the ordered placement language of the previous section; 'gift' renders χάρισμα as the sphere of one's appointed role.
rejected: just as he was set in his grace
just as he was appointed in his spiritual gift

choices.english: let the strong care for the weak
choices.why: τημελέω is a concrete verb of tending or looking after; 'care for' is plain and direct.
rejected: let the strong tend the weak
let the strong look after the weak

choices.term: ὁ δὲ ἀσθενὴς ἐντρεπέσθω τὸν ἰσχυρόν
choices.english: and let the weak respect the strong
choices.why: ἐντρέπω in the middle/passive means to show deference or regard; 'respect' captures the reciprocal social obligation without over-translating.
rejected: let the weak revere the strong
let the weak honor the strong

choices.english: let the rich supply the poor
choices.why: ἐπιχορηγέω means to furnish or provide for; 'supply' is concrete and matches the verb's sense of giving what is needed.
rejected: let the rich provide for the poor
let the rich give to the poor

pass_b_english: So let our whole body be kept safe in Christ Jesus, and let each person submit to his neighbor, just as each was placed in the gift God gave him.

Let the strong care for the weak, and let the weak respect the strong. Let the rich supply the poor, and let the poor give thanks to God, because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled. Let the wise show his wisdom not in words but in good works. Let the one who is humble not testify about himself, but let him allow another to testify about him. Let the one who is pure in the flesh not boast, knowing that another is the one who supplies him with self-control.

Let us consider, then, brothers, from what material we were made, what kind of persons we were when we entered the world, from what tomb and darkness the one who formed and created us brought us into his world, having prepared his benefits before we were born.
Since we have all these things from him, we ought to give thanks to him in everything. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: because he gave him someone through whom his lack might be filled
problems.source_quote: ὅτι ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ, δἰ οὗ ἀναπληρωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὸ ὑστέρημα
problems.why: δἰ οὗ refers to God (the giver), not 'someone'; God gave the poor person the means by which his lack is filled
problems.fix: because God gave to him the means by which his lack might be filled

edits.old: because he gave him someone through whom his lack might be filled
edits.new: because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled

problems.quote: just as he was placed in his gift
problems.source_quote: καθὼς ἐτέθη ἐν τῷ χαρίσματι αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Ambiguous: 'his' refers to God's gift, not the neighbor's. English suggests neighbor's gift.
problems.fix: just as each was placed in the gift God gave him
problems.ruling: καθὼς ἐτέθη ἐν τῷ χαρίσματι αὐτοῦ: 'his' is ambiguous; context (God's gift) needs clarification.

problems.quote: because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled
problems.source_quote: ὅτι ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ, δἰ οὗ ἀναπληρωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὸ ὑστέρημα
problems.why: Subject unclear: 'he' (the rich man) gave him, not God. The rich man is the supplier.
problems.fix: because he gave him the means by which his lack might be filled
problems.ruling: ὅτι ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ: subject is the rich man (ὁ πλούσιος), not God. 'God gave' misreads.

edits.new: just as each was placed in the gift God gave him

edits.old: because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled
edits.new: because he gave him the means by which his lack might be filled

fixed: Changed 'just as he was placed in his gift' to 'just as each was placed in the gift God gave him' to clarify that the gift is God's, not the neighbor's.
Changed 'because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled' to 'because he gave him the means by which his lack might be filled' to reflect that the rich man, not God, is the supplier.

problems.why: Glossary fixes 'humility' for ταπεινοφροσύνη; 'humble person' circumvents the required term.
problems.fix: Let the one of humility not bear witness to himself

edits.old: Let the humble person not bear witness to himself
edits.new: Let the one of humility not bear witness to himself

fixed: The glossary issue is real: 'humble person' circumvents the required term 'humility'. Changed to 'the one of humility'.

polish.changed: Clarified pronoun references, made the sequence of exhortations easier to follow aloud, and smoothed sentence rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'submission' for ὑποταγή family; 'submit' is the verb form but brief fixes 'submission' as English term.
last_rejected.fix: let each one show submission to his neighbor
last_rejected.ruling: ὑποτασσέσθω is a verb ('let him submit'); 'submit' correctly renders it. No glossary break or meaning change here.

last_rejected.quote: because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅτι ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ, δἰ οὗ ἀναπληρωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὸ ὑστέρημα
last_rejected.why: δι’ οὗ is a person God gave the poor (the rich), not an impersonal means.
last_rejected.fix: because God gave him someone through whom his lack might be filled
last_rejected.ruling: δι' οὗ with ἀναπληρωθῇ is neuter/masculine ambiguous; 'the means by which' is a normal rendering, and 'through whom' is a preference. Meaning (the rich supply the lack) is preserved.
